_comment: Worked example: the release v2.4 pyramid from pyramid-principle.md, built for a steering committee (11 slides + appendix). Image paths must exist before building - render them into presentations/assets/<slug>/ first.

meta.title: Release v2.4 delivery outlook
meta.subtitle: Monte Carlo forecast from 12 weeks of observed throughput

slides.notes: Ten minutes. The date is the news; everything after slide 2 is why.

slides.title: v2.4 will not make 15 October - plan for 1 November and decide what to cut
slides.statement: At the team's observed pace, v2.4 finishes 25 October at best and 1 November with the confidence a commitment needs - six weeks past the date currently on the roadmap.
supports: The remaining scope is 84 issues and the backlog has not shrunk in four weeks.
Throughput is stable at 8-9 issues per week, so there is no ramp to hope for.
Even the optimistic tail of 10,000 simulations lands after 15 October.
slides.takeaway: The choice is not whether to slip, but whether to slip the date or the scope.
slides.notes: Do not soften this. If they push back, the numbers are in the next three sections.

slides.title: The forecast in three numbers

kpis.label: P85 - the date worth committing to

slides.takeaway: Not one of 10,000 simulated futures finished by 15 October.

slides.statement: The remaining scope is 84 issues and it is not shrinking

slides.title: Open scope has been flat since mid-July despite steady delivery
slides.takeaway: Work is being closed at the same rate it is being added - the backlog is not converging.

slides.statement: Throughput is stable, so there is no recovery to plan around

slides.title: Twelve weeks of history show a steady team, not a slowing one

bullets.text: Weekly throughput sits between 6 and 11 issues with no trend
sub: Team-wide scope; release-only throughput is too thin to model.

bullets.text: No week in the window delivered enough to close a six-week gap
sub: Closing it needs roughly 14 issues per week, sustained.

bullets: Scope growth is modelled at 1.0 - any splits or discovered work make this worse, never better.
slides.takeaway: A stable team cannot absorb a six-week gap; only a scope or date decision can.

slides.statement: Every simulated future finishes after 15 October

slides.title: The percentile table leaves no reading that reaches 15 October
slides.takeaway: P85 - 1 November - is the date to put in front of the steering committee.

slides.title: Two options close the gap - and only one of them is free

left.heading: Move the date
bullets: Downstream launch dependencies shift six weeks

right.heading: Cut the scope
bullets: Removing ~40 issues brings P85 to mid-October
Needs a product call on which 40

slides.takeaway: Adding people is absent from this slide on purpose - it does not move a 10-week forecast.

slides.title: Three decisions this week keep the November date credible

steps.action: Confirm 1 November as the committed date, or authorise a scope cut
If cutting: nominate the 40 issues to drop from v2.4
Re-run the forecast after the decision and re-baseline

slides.takeaway: Every week without a decision moves both dates by a week.

slides.title: Method and assumptions
bullets: 10,000 trials, random seed 42, sampling weekly throughput with replacement
History window: last 12 complete weeks; team-wide throughput scope
Scope growth factor 1.0 - no allowance for splits or discovery
